name: Mull Thunderhorn
summary: In Bloodhoof Village, Mull Thunderhorn watches over Mulgore’s sacred wells. He serves the Earth Mother and guards the balance of the land. Outside exploitation threatens the waters, and he guides young tauren in cleansing the ancestral springs.

sections.title: Guardian of the Sacred Waters
sections.body: Mull Thunderhorn watches over Mulgore’s spiritual well-being from Bloodhoof Village. The nomadic tribes have gathered under High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof to make a permanent home, but greed and reckless expansion already threaten their lands. Mull guides young braves setting out from Camp Narache and calls on them to protect their ancestors’ vital resources.

sections.title: Tainted Wells and the Venture Company
sections.body: Mull Thunderhorn faces sickness in the Winterhoof, Thunderhorn, and Wildmane water wells. The corruption comes from goblins of the Venture Company, a commercial outfit cutting into the surrounding hills and pouring poisons into the local water table. Mull sends young tauren to prepare purification totems and cleanse each ancestral well before the corruption spreads through the land and its wildlife.

faq.answer: Mull Thunderhorn watches over the sacred water wells in Bloodhoof Village, Mulgore. He guides rites to keep the earth and its waters pure.

faq.q: Why is Mull Thunderhorn worried about the water wells?
faq.answer: The ancestral wells, including Winterhoof, Thunderhorn, and Wildmane, provide life-giving water for Mulgore’s tribes and wildlife. Nearby operations have tainted the springs with runoff and pollution, threatening the balance of the plains.

faq.q: Who is polluting the water wells in Mulgore?
faq.answer: Goblins of the Venture Company are polluting Mulgore’s water wells. The commercial outfit is establishing mining and logging operations around the edges of Mulgore, and its work sends toxins into the local water table.

faq.q: Why do Mull's purification quests only involve tauren?
faq.answer: Mulgore’s wells hold ancestral and spiritual meaning for the tauren tribes, including the Thunderhorn, Winterhoof, and Wildmane clans. Their cleansing is a sacred rite of passage and a duty for maturing tauren.

faq.q: How are the water wells purified?
faq.answer: Mull asks travelers to gather totems consecrated with offerings from the land, such as paws, talons, claws, and teeth from Mulgore’s beasts. The totems are brought to the fouled wells to channel spiritual cleansing and wash away unnatural toxins.

faq.q: What is the Rite of Vision?
faq.answer: The Rite of Vision is a spiritual journey for young tauren to commune with their ancestors and animal spirits. Initiates go to Zarlman Two-Moons in Bloodhoof Village for this visionary trial, one of the Rites of the Earthmother.

angles.text: For tauren, Mull Thunderhorn carries tribal memory and ancestral duty. He guides young braves in protecting the sacred plains from greedy outsiders.
As a shaman, you recognize Mull’s reliance on elemental harmony. His cleansing totems call on ancestral spirits to mend waters harmed by mechanical greed.
As a druid, you share Mull’s concern as corrupted wells poison the balance of Mulgore’s wildlife.
As a member of the Horde, you can see the strain between its people and unaligned organizations like the Venture Company, which takes Kalimdor’s riches without consent.
